title: Burst reservoir quotas and noisy tenant throttle playbook
creator: Priya Kannan
summary: Introduce a burst-reservoir quota layer and an operational playbook that automatically quarantines noisy tenants and applies proportional soft-throttles before hard-eviction. The goal is to provide predictable per-tenant throughput guarantees while reducing reactive evictions and improving tail latency during contention.
background: We've observed a growing number of P99 latency spikes during mixed workloads when individual tenants send short-lived bursts that exhaust shared lanes and trigger evictions.
Existing hard-slicing and soft-fencing mechanisms reduce impact but are coarse: they either allow short bursts to destabilize neighbours or immediately evict, which harms customer experience.
This ticket defines a middle-layer: per-tenant burst reservoirs (credit pools), noisy detection heuristics, and an automated quarantine+throttle flow tied to the autoscaler and eviction engine.
proposal: Allocate a small, configurable burst reservoir per tenant (credits expressed in GPU-ms or token-ops) that refills at a steady rate; burst consumption is charged against the reservoir before invoking quota penalties.
Implement a noisy-tenant detector that uses sliding-window KPIs (request rate, token rate, GPU util delta, per-lane latency increase) to classify tenants as normal/noisy/sustained-high.

Introduce a quarantine state: when a tenant is flagged noisy, place their requests into a quarantined lane with tight batching and an adaptive soft-throttle that reduces allowed concurrency rather than immediate eviction.
Emit eviction hints to the scheduler (adaptive-eviction-hints) so eviction scoring favors tenants that exhausted their reservoirs despite quarantining.
Integrate with autoscaling: when many tenants are in quarantine, trigger predictive scale-out suggestions rather than blind aggressive evictions.
design_decisions: Credit model: use GPU-ms as the canonical unit (maps cleanly to runtime cost), with default reservoir = 500 GPU-ms and refill rate = 50 GPU-ms/s. Values tunable per plan.
Quarantine duration: initial probation window 30s, with exponential backoff on repeated violations (30s -> 2m -> 8m).
Throttle behavior: proportional-concurrency cap (reduce concurrently executing streams by up to 70%) rather than outright request rejection, preserving best-effort throughput.
Detection thresholds: noisy if GPU-ms burn rate > 3x baseline AND lane P99 latency delta > 25% over a 60s window.
Rollout: start with Canary on a small Dedicated pool and an internal tenant cohort before broader release.
implementation_plan: 1) Runtime: add per-tenant reservoir accounting middleware and expose APIs to query reservoir state (GET /internal/tenants/{id}/reservoir).
2) Detector: implement sliding-window aggregator in telemetry service and publish noisy flags to the routing plane via the policy bus.
3) Quarantine lane: add a special execution lane optimized for high batching efficiency and soft-concurrency caps.
4) Eviction hints: extend scheduler RPC to accept eviction_hint priorities based on reservoir exhaustion and quarantine history.
5) Autoscaler integration: add a hook to recommend node add when >X% of tenants on a host are quarantined for >Ys.
6) Dashboarding: add per-tenant reservoir graphs and a quarantine dashboard in Console for SREs and SEs.
7) Tests & Chaos: run fault injections to validate quarantine doesn't cascade into systemic latencies.
risks: If reservoir sizing is too generous, noisy tenants can still impact neighbours; too small and paying customers will see throttles unexpectedly.
Quarantine lane misconfiguration could introduce higher average latency if batching parameters are not tuned for the cluster's mix.
Autoscaler chatter: aggressive scale suggestions from short-lived spikes could increase cost if not smoothed.
testing_plan: Unit tests for reservoir accounting (consumption, refill, concurrent drains).
Integration tests simulating mixed workloads with labeled synthetic tenants (bursting vs steady).
Load test: deploy canary to a 10-node dedicated pool and run 48h mixed-synthetic workload to monitor SLA adherence and eviction rates.
Chaos test: random network partitions and simulated slow GPUs to ensure quarantine doesn't amplify failures.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable feature for internal org + 3 partner tenants on two dedicated pools (1 week).
Phase 2 (limited GA): opt-in for customers on dedicated plans with console toggle + migration docs (2 weeks).
Phase 3 (default): enable for new dedicated clusters with conservative defaults; expose reservoir sizing in console (4 weeks).
metrics: Primary: eviction_rate_per_host (reduce by 40% target during contention windows).
Primary: tenant_p99_latency_delta (target < 10% increase compared to baseline).
Cost: autoscale_suggestions_triggered and actual_scale_actions (to detect oscillations).
acceptance_criteria: Canary demonstrates >30% reduction in eviction_rate_per_host during controlled bursts compared to baseline.
No critical customer reports during the 2-week limited GA; SRE postmortem shows quarantine reduced manual evictions.
Console shows per-tenant reservoir graphs and SREs can toggle quarantine mitigation per-cluster.
Documentation and runbook completed: quarantine playbook, tuning guide, and rollback steps.

notes: This ticket intentionally steers away from immediate hard quota enforcement; the philosophy is to buy time (soft mitigation + reservoir) and surface clearer signals to the autoscaler and ops.
Billing implications: we will surface consumed reservoir as a line-item in billing exports for transparency; final pricing decision deferred to PM.
